newsitem.title: USA: US money managers remain bullish on US debt - MCM.
newsitem.headline: US money managers remain bullish on US debt - MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers slightly extended durations of their U.S. debt portfolios over the past week, an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey said.
The survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 108.2 percent in the week ending May 12 from 108.0 in the prior week.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 28 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," compared with 33 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 14 percent, against 10 percent the week ended May 5.
Fifty-eight percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 3.02 percent, against 3.06 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 33 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, unchanged from the previous week, while 9 percent underweighted it. The remaining 58 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 40 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 19 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
